newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm as battered Dadas rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm as battered Dadas rebounds.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 0.36 percent on Thursday, pulled up by a rebound in battered financial consultancy Dadas after the company reported a better-than-expected first-half result.

"The mood on the market today was very optimistic. Dadas' results were much better than expected, and some foreign capital also entered our market after newly listed shares of drug maker Lek were listed," said Davor Dubokovic, a trader at Eastbrokers.
Dadas on Thursday said net profit in the first six months tumbled to 42.3 million tolars from 86 million a year ago.

He added the market was likely to continue rising on Friday, reversing a 5.2 percent fall earlier this week when investors were rattled by rumours Dadas may face bankruptcy and its brokerage arm could be banned from trading.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 3.25 points to 912.89.
* 10 shares rose and six fell, while eight were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 162.9 million tolars from 140 million.
* Lek's newly listed shares were the most actively traded issue for the second day in a row, firming 1.09 percent to 13,918 tolars on volume of 6,980 shares for total turnover of 97.2 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Dadas was the biggest gainer, firming 13.98 percent to 14,603 tolars on volume of 1,330 shares for total turnover of 19.4 million tolars.

* Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner, falling 7.07 percent to 15,240 tolars on volume of 35 shares for total turnover of 533,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
